      "kind": "p",
      "text": "Relatively few kinds of material in nature are ferromagnetic, but they have important practical uses.\n\nAt a temperature below the material's Curie temperature, inserting a suitable iron or steel core can greatly strengthen the field inside a coil while its current and winding geometry remain the same.\n\nThe extra field comes from the magnetized material, not from an increase in coil current;\nthe enhancement also depends on the material, its shape, and its magnetic state.",

      "source_text": "虽然在自然界中铁磁性物体并不多，但是它却具有很大的实际意义. 把铁芯或钢芯插到线圈中时，不增大线圈中的电流，就可以使通电线圈产生的磁场增大很多倍.",

      "text": "Under suitable magnetizing conditions, a ferromagnetic material can become magnetized along the applied field, and its relative permeability $\\mu$ can be much greater than 1.\n\nAfter magnetization, some ferromagnetic specimens retain a net magnetization when the applied magnetizing field is removed;\nthis is remanence.\n\nRemanence is not evidence that current is still flowing in the coil, nor does it mean that every unmagnetized piece is already a permanent magnet.",

      "source_refs": [

      ],
      "source_text": "前面曾讲过，铁磁质可以沿着场的方向被磁化，它的 $\\mu$ 值远远大于 1. 此外，铁磁性物体具有剩磁.",

    {
      "kind": "p",
      "text": "The permeability of a ferromagnetic material is not a fixed material constant.\n\nEven at the same temperature and with the same specimen shape, it depends on the present field strength and on the specimen's previous magnetizing history.\n\nKnowing only the present applied field is therefore often insufficient to determine the magnetic state;\niron cannot be assigned a single enhancement factor valid in every situation.",

      "label": null,
      "printed_page": 319,
      "source_refs": [
        "p0328#3"
      ],
      "source_text": "铁磁质的磁导率不是一个恒量. 它与磁场的强弱有关.同时，不仅与这个时刻的磁场有关，而且还与前一个时刻对物质作用的磁场有关. 下面，较详细地讨论这一点.",

    {
      "kind": "p",
      "text": "Heating a ferromagnetic material above its particular Curie temperature removes its ferromagnetic spontaneous magnetization, not every possible response to a magnetic field.\n\nThe temperature is named after the French scientist Curie (居里);\n\nan iron needle heated sufficiently above this temperature loses the conspicuous ability to attract iron that came from its remanent magnetization.\n\nThe original textbook lists iron at $753^\\circ\\mathrm{C}$, nickel at $365^\\circ\\mathrm{C}$, and cobalt at $1000^\\circ\\mathrm{C}$;\n\nsome ferromagnetic alloys have Curie temperatures below $100^\\circ\\mathrm{C}$.\nThese numbers are retained as the textbook's reported values, not as modern precision measurements;\n\na particular material's transition temperature must be established from its composition and measurement data.",

      "source_refs": [

      "source_text": "当温度高于某种铁磁性物质的特定温度时，它的磁性就消失. 这个温度叫做居里温度（以发现这个现象的法国学者居里的名字命名的）. 如果给磁化了的铁针强烈地加热，它就丧失了吸引铁物体的能力. 铁的居里温度为 $753^\\circ\\mathrm{C}$，镍为$365^\\circ\\mathrm{C}$，而钴为 $1000^\\circ\\mathrm{C}$. 一些铁磁性的合金的居里温度小于$100^\\circ\\mathrm{C}$.",

      "kind": "p",
      "text": "To describe the material's magnetic state, this textbook introduces a quantity called **magnetization**.\n\nConsider a long, uniform iron rod inside a sufficiently long solenoid, using a model in which the central fields are approximately uniform and aligned and end-related demagnetizing effects are negligible;\n\nat a specified nonzero applied field and magnetic history, write the internal flux density as $B=\\mu B_0$.\n\nHere $B$ is the total internal magnetic flux density with the material present, while $B_0$ is the flux density produced by the same coil current without the material;\n\ntheir difference measures the material's magnetic contribution.\n\nThe textbook denotes this difference by $I$, so it has units of magnetic flux density, not electric current and not the amperes-per-metre units commonly used for modern magnetization;\n\nconversion between the magnetic quantities involves the permeability of free space.\n\nThe relative permeability here describes a ratio at the specified state, not a constant valid for all fields and histories.",

      "source_refs": [

      ],

      "text": "The relation between $I$ and $B_0$ is complex because a ferromagnet's $\\mu$ itself depends on $B_0$, as well as on magnetic history.\n\nFor a specified temperature, specimen shape, and magnetizing procedure, the curve showing $I$ against $B_0$ is called a **magnetization curve**.\n\nIt can be obtained experimentally using the measurement approach in §133;\ndifferent procedures need not produce the same curve.",

    {
      "kind": "p",
      "text": "Start with a demagnetized iron specimen whose net magnetization is approximately zero, keep its temperature fixed below the Curie temperature, and increase the applied field slowly;\n\ninitially, its magnetization $I$ rises approximately linearly with $B_0$, as shown in Figure 301.\n\nThe specimen then approaches saturation: although $B_0$ continues to increase, the material's magnetic contribution becomes nearly constant, but the total internal field need not stop increasing.\n\nThe textbook explains this using the orientation of tiny loop currents: at saturation, their magnetic moments are nearly aligned with the field, so further increases in $B_0$ cannot substantially increase their contribution.\n\nThis is a qualitative magnetic-moment model, not a picture of electron spin as a mechanically rotating ball;\n\nin domain language, existing spontaneously magnetized regions change their sizes and orientations, increasing the net magnetization until it approaches aligned saturation.",

      "source_text": "从实验得到下列结果. 如果铁样品事先没有被磁化，则在开始时，磁化强度 $I$ 随着 $B_0$ 的增大几乎按直线规律增大（图 301）. 但是，后来达到饱和状态：尽管 $B_0$ 继续增大，而磁化强度保持不变. 这里，可以假设：当饱和状态时，所有的环形电流完全按场的方向取向，从而随着 $B_0$ 的继续增大，由它们产生的场不再改变. 事实上也是这样.",

    {
      "kind": "p",
      "text": "The actual relation between $I$ and $B_0$ is more complex than the initial curve in Figure 301: the same present field can correspond to different magnetic states.\n\nMagnetization depends on whether the specimen was magnetized before, how strong the previous field was, and how it increased or decreased;\n\nFigure 301 describes only increasing the field from a demagnetized state.\n\nAt the same temperature and specimen geometry, with a slowly changing field, reducing the magnetizing field from saturation does not make the magnetization $I$ retrace the increasing-field curve;\n\nit usually retains a larger magnetization.\nThis dependence on magnetic history is **hysteresis**;\n\ndomain-wall motion and magnetic-moment reorientation can be impeded, so removing the applied field need not restore the initial state.",
      "id": null,

      "printed_page": 320,
      "source_refs": [
        "p0329#6"
      ],
      "source_text": "实际上，$I$ 和 $B_0$ 的关系比图 301 所示的要复杂些. 问题在于：这个关系不是单值的. 磁化强度不仅与这个时刻的磁场有关，而且与前一个时刻它的量值是多少有关. 图 301 上所示的曲线，只是在铁样品事先没被磁化的情况下得到的. 达到饱和状态以后，当磁化场减小时，磁化强度 $I$ 减小得比它增长时要慢. 这种现象叫做磁滞现象.",

      "kind": "p",
      "text": "Figure 302 shows a full magnetizing sequence relating $I$ and $B_0$;\n\nkeep temperature and specimen shape fixed, neglect background fields, and change the applied magnetizing field slowly.\n\nStarting from a demagnetized state, increase the field along $oa$, as on the initial magnetization curve in Figure 301, and reach approximate saturation at $a$.\n\nThen reduce $B_0$ to 0, following $ab$;\nwhen $B_0=0$, the magnetization is still nonzero, and $I=ob$ represents **remanence**.\n\nWith the applied magnetizing field removed, the specimen still produces its own field and behaves as a permanent magnet;\n\nthis comes from retained material magnetization, not continuing coil current, and it does not mean the total internal field is zero.\n\nA finite, constant permeability multiplied by a zero applied field cannot be used here to rule out remanence.\n\nNext, increase the applied magnetic flux density $B_0$ in the reverse direction until the net magnetization reaches zero at the textbook's $B_{0k}=oc$;\n\nthe plotted distance expresses the magnitude of the reverse field, not a claim that its direction is positive.\n\nThe textbook calls $B_{0k}$ the **coercive field**, expressing the reverse magnetizing-field scale needed to reduce this specimen's net magnetization to zero;\n\nit is not a mechanical force or the total internal magnetic flux density, and conversion is needed to the field-strength units commonly used today.\n\nContinue to reverse saturation at $a'$, reduce the field to zero, then increase it in the original direction until the curve returns to $a$.\n\nIn an ideal model with fixed temperature, no magnetic bias, and equivalent forward and reverse procedures, this closed curve is symmetric about $o$ and is called a **hysteresis loop**.",

      "source_text": "$I$ 和 $B_0$ 的关系的一般特性，如图 302 所示. 线段 $oa$ 是类似于图 301 上的磁化曲线. 在 $a$ 点达到饱和. 当 $B_0$ 减小到 0 时，磁化强度减小，这相应于曲线的 $ab$段. 当 $B_0=0$ 时，磁化强度不等于零. 它的量值 $I=ob$ 是**剩磁**. 在没有外界磁化场时，铁样品仍产生磁场. 因此，它是永久磁铁. 当在相反的方向增大磁感应强度 $B_0$ 时，磁化强度减小，只有当 $B_{0k}=oc$ 时，磁化强度才等于零. 量 $B_{0k}$ 叫做**矫顽力**. 这是使样品去磁所需的磁感应强度. 在 $a'$ 点，样品重新被磁化到饱和状态，但方向相反. 减小磁场到零，并又重新增大到饱和（点 $a$）时，得到相对于 $o$ 点对称的闭合曲线，叫做**磁滞回线**.",

      "text": "The original textbook credits the Russian physicist A. G. Stoletov (斯托列托夫, 1839-1896) as the first to study the magnetizing characteristics of ferromagnetic materials carefully.\n\nA. Stoletov used a magnetizing method in which wire was wound around a closed iron ring and current was passed through the wire to magnetize the ring.\n\nA closed magnetic path helps reduce the end-related demagnetizing effects of an open rod;\n\nthe coil's magnetizing field establishes the material's magnetization, which must not be mistaken for electric current in the wire.",

      "text": "Different ferromagnetic materials can have differently shaped hysteresis loops, an important basis for comparing their magnetic properties.\n\nSuch comparisons require specified temperatures, specimen shapes, magnetic histories, and field-changing conditions;\na loop is not a fixed shape independent of the experiment.",

      "kind": "p",
      "text": "Ferromagnetic materials may be classified as **magnetically soft** or **magnetically hard** according to how easily they are magnetized and demagnetized;\n\nthis is not mechanical hardness.\n\nWith the same axis scales and comparable magnetizing conditions, Figure 303a illustrates a narrower, smaller-area soft-material loop, with smaller remanence and coercivity in this particular drawing.\n\nIron, certain steels, and permalloy, an iron-nickel alloy, can be magnetically soft;\n\nthese materials readily reverse their magnetization, but a small loop area alone does not establish small remanence for every soft material.\n\nFigure 303b illustrates a wider, larger-area hard-material loop, with larger remanence and coercivity in this drawing.\n\nStable remanence and greater resistance to demagnetization make such materials suitable for permanent magnets;\n\ncomparisons must still specify temperature, magnetizing amplitude, and specimen conditions.",
      "id": null,
      "label": null,
      "printed_page": 321,
      "source_refs": [
        "p0330#4"
      ],
      "source_text": "按磁性把材料分为“软”磁物质和“硬”磁物质. 软磁物质的回线面积小（图 303а），因此，剩磁和矫顽力都小. 属于这种物质的有：铁、个别品种的钢，坡莫合金（铁镍合金）等. 硬磁物质的回线面积大（图 303б），剩磁和矫顽力都大.因此，可用这些材料制作永久磁铁.",

      "kind": "p",
      "text": "Magnetically soft materials can serve as cores in transformers, generators, and electric motors.\n\nUnder operating conditions that require alternating magnetic fields, the core is repeatedly magnetized and demagnetized, requiring external work;\n\nsome energy becomes heat during each hysteresis cycle.\n\nFor a complete, sufficiently slow cycle at fixed temperature and specimen conditions, the enclosed loop area, converted using the correct physical axes and units, represents hysteresis energy loss per unit material volume per cycle;\n\nbecause this textbook expresses magnetization as a flux-density contribution, conversion involving the permeability of free space is needed, and the whole core's loss also depends on its volume.\n\nAn area measured on the page is not directly the work done on the entire core.\n\nAt the same magnetizing amplitude and under comparable conditions, a narrower-loop soft material usually has less hysteresis loss than a wider-loop hard material;\n\nactual devices also have losses such as eddy-current loss, so loop area alone does not determine their total loss.",
      "id": null,

      "printed_title": "134. 铁磁质的基本性质",

      "prose": [
        {
          "kind": "p",
          "text": "虽然在自然界中铁磁性物体并不多，但是它却具有很大的实际意义. 把铁芯或钢芯插到线圈中时，不增大线圈中的电流，就可以使通电线圈产生的磁场增大很多倍.",
          "id": null,
          "label": null,
          "printed_page": 318,
          "source_refs": [
            "p0327#9",
            "p0328#1"
          ]
        },
        {
          "kind": "p",
          "text": "前面曾讲过，铁磁质可以沿着场的方向被磁化，它的 $\\mu$ 值远远大于 1. 此外，铁磁性物体具有剩磁.",
          "id": null,
          "label": null,
          "printed_page": 319,
          "source_refs": [
            "p0328#2"
          ]
        },
        {
          "kind": "p",
          "text": "铁磁质的磁导率不是一个恒量. 它与磁场的强弱有关.同时，不仅与这个时刻的磁场有关，而且还与前一个时刻对物质作用的磁场有关. 下面，较详细地讨论这一点.",
          "id": null,
          "label": null,
          "printed_page": 319,
          "source_refs": [
            "p0328#3"
          ]
        },
        {
          "kind": "p",
          "text": "当温度高于某种铁磁性物质的特定温度时，它的磁性就消失. 这个温度叫做居里温度（以发现这个现象的法国学者居里的名字命名的）. 如果给磁化了的铁针强烈地加热，它就丧失了吸引铁物体的能力. 铁的居里温度为 $753^\\circ\\mathrm{C}$，镍为$365^\\circ\\mathrm{C}$，而钴为 $1000^\\circ\\mathrm{C}$. 一些铁磁性的合金的居里温度小于$100^\\circ\\mathrm{C}$.",
          "id": null,
          "label": null,
          "printed_page": 319,
          "source_refs": [
            "p0328#4"
          ]
        },
        {
          "kind": "p",
          "text": "利用叫做**磁化强度**的量来表征铁磁质的磁性状态是比较方便的. 如果把长的均匀铁棒放在螺线管的内部，则它内部的磁感应强度等于 $B=\\mu B_0$. $B$ 和 $B_0$ 之差可以作为材料的磁化强度的量度. 磁化强度 $I$ 等于：",
          "id": null,
          "label": null,
          "printed_page": 319,
          "source_refs": [
            "p0328#5"
          ]
        },
        {
          "kind": "p",
          "text": "$I=B-B_0$　　(13-2)",
          "id": null,
          "label": null,
          "printed_page": 319,
          "source_refs": [
            "p0328#6"
          ]
        },
        {
          "kind": "p",
          "text": "或，考虑到(13-1)式，",
          "id": null,
          "label": null,
          "printed_page": 319,
          "source_refs": [
            "p0328#7"
          ]
        },
        {
          "kind": "p",
          "text": "$I=(\\mu-1)B_0$.　　(13-3)",
          "id": null,
          "label": null,
          "printed_page": 319,
          "source_refs": [
            "p0328#8"
          ]
        },
        {
          "kind": "p",
          "text": "$I$ 和 $B_0$ 的关系是很复杂的，因为铁磁质的 $\\mu$ 与 $B_0$ 有关.$I$ 和 $B_0$ 的关系叫做所谓的**磁化曲线**，磁化曲线可以由实验求出（参阅 §133）.",
          "id": null,
          "label": null,
          "printed_page": 319,
          "source_refs": [
            "p0328#9"
          ]
        },
        {
          "kind": "p",
          "text": "从实验得到下列结果. 如果铁样品事先没有被磁化，则在开始时，磁化强度 $I$ 随着 $B_0$ 的增大几乎按直线规律增大（图 301）. 但是，后来达到饱和状态：尽管 $B_0$ 继续增大，而磁化强度保持不变. 这里，可以假设：当饱和状态时，所有的环形电流完全按场的方向取向，从而随着 $B_0$ 的继续增大，由它们产生的场不再改变. 事实上也是这样.",
          "id": null,
          "label": null,
          "printed_page": 319,
          "source_refs": [
            "p0328#10",
            "p0329#1",
            "p0329#4"
          ]
        },
        {
          "kind": "fig",
          "text": "",
          "id": "fig-301",
          "label": "图 301",
          "printed_page": 320,
          "source_refs": [
            "p0329#2"
          ]
        },
        {
          "kind": "cap",
          "text": "图 301",
          "id": null,
          "label": "图 301",
          "printed_page": 320,
          "source_refs": [
            "p0329#3"
          ]
        },
        {
          "kind": "p",
          "text": "应当强调指出：每一种铁磁质，是用自己的磁化曲线来表示的.",
          "id": null,
          "label": null,
          "printed_page": 320,
          "source_refs": [
            "p0329#5"
          ]
        },
        {
          "kind": "p",
          "text": "实际上，$I$ 和 $B_0$ 的关系比图 301 所示的要复杂些. 问题在于：这个关系不是单值的. 磁化强度不仅与这个时刻的磁场有关，而且与前一个时刻它的量值是多少有关. 图 301 上所示的曲线，只是在铁样品事先没被磁化的情况下得到的. 达到饱和状态以后，当磁化场减小时，磁化强度 $I$ 减小得比它增长时要慢. 这种现象叫做磁滞现象.",
          "id": null,
          "label": null,
          "printed_page": 320,
          "source_refs": [
            "p0329#6"
          ]
        },
        {
          "kind": "p",
          "text": "$I$ 和 $B_0$ 的关系的一般特性，如图 302 所示. 线段 $oa$ 是类似于图 301 上的磁化曲线. 在 $a$ 点达到饱和. 当 $B_0$ 减小到 0 时，磁化强度减小，这相应于曲线的 $ab$段. 当 $B_0=0$ 时，磁化强度不等于零. 它的量值 $I=ob$ 是**剩磁**. 在没有外界磁化场时，铁样品仍产生磁场. 因此，它是永久磁铁. 当在相反的方向增大磁感应强度 $B_0$ 时，磁化强度减小，只有当 $B_{0k}=oc$ 时，磁化强度才等于零. 量 $B_{0k}$ 叫做**矫顽力**. 这是使样品去磁所需的磁感应强度. 在 $a'$ 点，样品重新被磁化到饱和状态，但方向相反. 减小磁场到零，并又重新增大到饱和（点 $a$）时，得到相对于 $o$ 点对称的闭合曲线，叫做**磁滞回线**.",
          "id": null,
          "label": null,
          "printed_page": 320,
          "source_refs": [
            "p0329#7",
            "p0329#10",
            "p0330#1"
          ]
        },
        {
          "kind": "fig",
          "text": "",
          "id": "fig-302",
          "label": "图 302",
          "printed_page": 320,
          "source_refs": [
            "p0329#8"
          ]
        },
        {
          "kind": "cap",
          "text": "图 302",
          "id": null,
          "label": "图 302",
          "printed_page": 320,
          "source_refs": [
            "p0329#9"
          ]
        },
        {
          "kind": "p",
          "text": "第一个仔细研究铁磁性材料的磁化强度的，是杰出的俄国学者 А. Г. 斯托列托夫（1839～1896）. А. Г. 斯托列托夫第一个应用了磁化的方法，他给缠在闭合铁环上的导线通以电流，从而使闭合的铁环磁化.",
          "id": null,
          "label": null,
          "printed_page": 321,
          "source_refs": [
            "p0330#2"
          ]
        },
        {
          "kind": "p",
          "text": "不同的铁磁性材料，具有不同形状的磁滞回线. 回线的形状是铁磁性材料的重要特性.",
          "id": null,
          "label": null,
          "printed_page": 321,
          "source_refs": [
            "p0330#3"
          ]
        },
        {
          "kind": "p",
          "text": "按磁性把材料分为“软”磁物质和“硬”磁物质. 软磁物质的回线面积小（图 303а），因此，剩磁和矫顽力都小. 属于这种物质的有：铁、个别品种的钢，坡莫合金（铁镍合金）等. 硬磁物质的回线面积大（图 303б），剩磁和矫顽力都大.因此，可用这些材料制作永久磁铁.",
          "id": null,
          "label": null,
          "printed_page": 321,
          "source_refs": [
            "p0330#4"
          ]
        },
        {
          "kind": "p",
          "text": "软磁材料用来作变压器、发电机、电动机等的铁芯. 根据工作条件，铁芯经常不断地用交变磁场反复磁化，反复磁化时需要做功，功的数值等于磁滞回线所包围的面积. 因此，软磁物质比硬磁物质的能量损失少.",
          "id": null,
          "label": null,
          "printed_page": 321,
          "source_refs": [
            "p0330#5"
          ]
        },
